title: KumoMTA: What Running Your Own Mail Transfer Agent Requires
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: A campaign application chooses recipients and content. An MTA handles SMTP delivery and retries. KumoMTA is an option for the delivery layer; this article is an architecture guide, not confirmation that a particular Laravel Mail installation is using it.
content:
Separate campaign management from delivery

A campaign application chooses recipients and content. An MTA handles SMTP delivery and retries. KumoMTA is an option for the delivery layer; this article is an architecture guide, not confirmation that a particular Laravel Mail installation is using it.

Configure traffic shaping

KumoMTA documents destination-specific connection limits and sending rates. Its documentation warns that unrestricted delivery is unwelcome to many mailbox providers. Do not treat the default configuration as a ready-made deliverability policy.

Understand the queues

Scheduled queues hold messages awaiting delivery or retry. Ready queues and egress paths handle delivery work. KumoMTA documents separate controls for retry intervals, message age and traffic shaping. Test these settings against your requirements.

Keep the operational checks

DNS, authentication, bounce processing, monitoring and abuse handling are your responsibility when you run the delivery service. Start with consented, limited-volume test traffic. Owning the MTA provides controls, not a guarantee that recipients will receive or read the message.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
